title: FastOmniTMAE: Parallel Clause Learning for Scalable and Hardware-Efficient Tsetlin Embeddings
new_feature: Reformulates Omni TM-AE word-embedding training by removing the global class_sum dependency: each clause computes its update probability locally, so evaluation and update run in parallel per clause. Implemented as a reusable SoC-FPGA training accelerator IP (Zynq-7000 Zybo, Zynq UltraScale+ ZCU104) and benchmarked against CPU, OpenCL and CUDA builds.

datasets.split_as_reported: Embedding training corpus. Classification test: 100 target tokens, 1,000 training examples per token then 500 examples for inference; hardware benchmark: 8,000 prepared examples per token (44 tokens, 352k examples)
datasets.booleanization: bag-of-words over 40k-token vocabulary (+ negations = 80k literals); input X accumulates a documents
datasets.notes: Per-token binary target-presence classification used to compare FastOmniTMAE vs Omni TM-AE; also source corpus for all word-similarity embeddings.

extraction_notes: Classification-task precision/recall/F1 curves only in Fig. 4 (not tabulated); only the text-stated Omni TM-AE final F1 (0.56) and training times are recorded. Average similarity scores (Table 1 'Avg.') are attached to dataset_id one-billion-word. RG-65 standardly has 65 pairs, but the paper describes its RG65 workload as 44 tokens / '44 word pairs'. Code will be released after review (no URL). Table 3 FPGA resource counts recorded with unit 'count'.
